title: Reading Stories
description: Learn to read and understand simple English stories.
competenceGoals: read and understand simple texts in English

content.content:
## Reading Stories in English

Reading stories in English is fun and helps you learn new words! When you read, you travel to new places and meet interesting characters.

**Why read in English?**
- You learn new words
- You see how sentences are built
- You have fun!

content.title: Parts of a Story
content.content:
Every story has three main parts:

**Beginning** - We meet the characters and learn where the story takes place.

**Middle** - Something happens! There is often a problem to solve.

**End** - The problem is solved and the story finishes.

## Tips for Reading

**Before you read:**
- Look at the pictures
- Read the title
- Think: What might happen?

**While you read:**
- Read slowly
- Look at the pictures for help
- Don't stop at every new word

**After you read:**
- Think: What happened?
- What was your favorite part?

content.title: Using Context
content.content:
**Context** means the words around a word you don't know. You can often guess what a word means by looking at the other words!

**Example:**
"The cat was very hungry. It ate all the food quickly."

If you don't know "hungry", you can guess: The cat ate all the food, so "hungry" must mean it wanted food!

content.title: Example: Understanding a Short Story
content.problem:
Read this short text:

"Tom had a little dog called Max. Max liked to run and play in the garden. One day, Max found a big bone. He was so happy!"
content.solution:
**Who is in the story?** Tom and his dog Max

**Where does it happen?** In the garden

**What happens?** Max finds a big bone and is happy

**New words you might learn:**
- garden = hage
- bone = bein
- found = fant

exercise.task: What are the three parts of a story?
hints: Think about when things happen in a story

exercise.task: Read this sentence and guess what "tired" means: "After running all day, the boy was very tired and went to bed early."
exercise.solution: "Tired" means trøtt. The boy ran all day and went to bed early, so he must have been sleepy and needed rest.
hints: What would you feel like after running all day?

exercise.task:
Read this short story and answer the questions:

"Sara woke up early on Saturday. Today was her birthday! She ran downstairs. Her family was waiting with a big cake and presents. Sara smiled and said thank you."

subTasks.label: b
subTasks.solution: It is her birthday and her family has cake and presents.

hints: Read the story carefully and find the answers

content.content:
## Oppsummering

I dette kapittelet har du lært:

- **Story parts**: Every story has a beginning, a middle, and an end.
- **Reading tips**: Look at the title and pictures before you read, and read slowly.
- **Context**: You can guess what a new word means from the words around it.

### Husk!
- A story = beginning + middle + end.
- Don't stop at every new word - use the context to guess!

Read this sentence and guess what 'enormous' means: 'The elephant was so enormous it could not fit through the door.'
exercise.solution: 'Enormous' means kjempestor/veldig stor. The elephant could not fit through the door, so it must be very big.
